title_zh: 伯里克利胸像（大英博物馆）
object: Marble bust of Pericles, Roman copy (2nd c. AD) after a Greek original of c. 440–430 BC attributed to Kresilas; from Hadrian's Villa, Tivoli. British Museum, London, GR 1805,0703.91 (Townley Collection).
author: Marie-Lan Nguyen (Jastrow)
attribution_text: Photo: Marie-Lan Nguyen / CC BY 2.5, via Wikimedia Commons

title_zh: 伯里克利胸像（梵蒂冈，带铭文“伯里克利，克桑西普斯之子，雅典人”）
title_en: Bust of Pericles with inscription (Vatican Museums)
object: Marble herm-bust of Pericles inscribed ΠΕΡΙΚΛΗΣ ΞΑΝΘΙΠΠΟΥ ΑΘΗΝΑΙΟΣ (“Pericles, son of Xanthippus, Athenian”), Roman copy after a Greek original of c. 430 BC (Kresilas type). Museo Pio-Clementino, Sala delle Muse, Vatican Museums, Inv. 269.
author: Jastrow (Marie-Lan Nguyen)
attribution_text: Photo: Jastrow / Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons

title_zh: 修昔底德头像（皇家安大略博物馆）
object: Marble portrait head of Thucydides, Roman/late Hellenistic copy of a lost Greek portrait of the early 4th c. BC (same type as the Holkham Hall bust). Royal Ontario Museum, Toronto. Background removed by the photographer.
author: Captmondo
attribution_text: Photo: Captmondo / Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons

title_zh: 希罗多德与修昔底德双面胸像（那不勒斯）
title_en: Double herm of Herodotus and Thucydides (Naples)
object: Roman marble double herm of Herodotus and Thucydides, inscribed with both names; Farnese Collection. Museo Archeologico Nazionale di Napoli, inv. 6239.
author: Yair Haklai
attribution_text: Photo: Yair Haklai / CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

title_zh: 所谓“亚西比德”胸像（卡比托利欧博物馆）
object: Idealised male portrait traditionally identified as Alcibiades; Roman copy after a Greek original of the 4th c. BC. The herm shaft and the inscription “Alcibiades, son of Cleinias, Athenian” are modern additions, so the identification is not secure. Palazzo dei Conservatori, Capitoline Museums, Rome, MC 1160.
author: Jastrow (Marie-Lan Nguyen)
attribution_text: Photo: Jastrow / Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons

title_zh: 雅典四德拉克马银币（正面：雅典娜）
title_en: Athenian silver tetradrachm, obverse: head of Athena
object: Silver tetradrachm minted at Athens, 449–440 BC; obverse: head of Athena right in crested Attic helmet with olive leaves. Cleveland Museum of Art, 1941.296 (Gift of Dr. Jacob Hirsch).
author: Cleveland Museum of Art
attribution_text: Cleveland Museum of Art, Gift of Dr. Jacob Hirsch / CC0

title_zh: 雅典四德拉克马银币（背面：猫头鹰）
object: Silver tetradrachm minted at Athens, 449–440 BC; reverse: owl standing right, olive sprig and crescent moon, legend ΑΘΕ. Cleveland Museum of Art, 1941.296 (Gift of Dr. Jacob Hirsch).
author: Cleveland Museum of Art
attribution_text: Cleveland Museum of Art, Gift of Dr. Jacob Hirsch / CC0

title_zh: 勒诺尔芒浮雕：三列桨战舰与桨手（卫城博物馆）
title_en: Lenormant Relief: trireme with rowers (Acropolis Museum)
object: Marble votive relief fragments showing the oarsmen of an Athenian trireme (identified as the state ship Paralos), shown against a drawn reconstruction; late 5th c. BC. Acropolis Museum, Athens, Acr. 1339.
author: Ad Meskens
attribution_text: Photo: © Ad Meskens / Wikimedia Commons / CC BY-SA 4.0

title_zh: 复原三列桨战舰“奥林匹亚斯”号
object: The Olympias, a full-size reconstruction of an ancient Athenian trireme built in 1985–1987 (design by J. S. Morrison, J. F. Coates and others), moored at Flisvos Marina, Palaio Faliro, Attica. Photographed 23 February 2019.
author: George E. Koronaios
attribution_text: Photo: George E. Koronaios / CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

title_zh: 刻有地米斯托克利名字的陶片
object: Group of ostraka (inscribed potsherds) cast against Themistocles, from a deposit found in a well on the north slope of the Acropolis; early 5th c. BC (the source description dates them to 482 BC). Ancient Agora Museum, Athens.
author: Sharon Mollerus
attribution_text: Photo: Sharon Mollerus / CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons

title_zh: 刻有伯里克利名字的陶片
object: Ostrakon inscribed with the name of Pericles, son of Xanthippus (ΠΕΡΙΚΛΕΣ ΧΣΑΝΘΙΠΠΟ); mid-5th c. BC. Ancient Agora Museum, Athens.
author: wallyg (Flickr)
attribution_text: Photo: wallyg / CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons

title_zh: 斯巴达重装步兵像（所谓“列奥尼达”）
object: Marble statue of a helmeted hoplite known as “Leonidas”, 480–470 BC, from the Sanctuary of Athena Chalkioikos on the acropolis of Sparta. Archaeological Museum of Sparta, inv. 3365. The identification with Leonidas is traditional, not proven.
author: Mary Harrsch
attribution_text: Photo: Mary Harrsch / CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

title_zh: 科林斯式青铜头盔
object: Bronze Corinthian helmet from the tomb of the warrior Denda; Greek workshop in South Italy, 500–490 BC. Staatliche Antikensammlungen, Munich, Inv. 4330.
author: Daderot
attribution_text: Photo: Daderot / CC0, via Wikimedia Commons

title_zh: 阿提卡红绘陶罐：出征的重装步兵
object: Attic red-figure stamnos attributed to the Berlin Painter, ca. 490 BC: a hoplite with shield and spear between a woman and a seated old man (warrior-departure scene). Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York, 1988.40.
author: Metropolitan Museum of Art
attribution_text: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Gift of Christos G. Bastis, 1988 / CC0

title_zh: 阿提卡红绘双耳罐：战士出征
object: Attic red-figure belly amphora by the Kleophrades Painter, 500–490 BC, from Vulci; side A: a young warrior arming/departing, with a woman holding a phiale and an old man. Staatliche Antikensammlungen, Munich, Inv. 2305.
author: Bibi Saint-Pol
attribution_text: Photo: Bibi Saint-Pol / Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons

title_zh: 叙拉古采石场（天堂采石场）
object: The Latomia del Paradiso, an ancient limestone quarry in the Neapolis archaeological park, Syracuse, Sicily — the kind of quarry where Athenian prisoners were held after 413 BC. Photographed 2009.
author: Sailko
attribution_text: Photo: Sailko / CC BY 2.5, via Wikimedia Commons

title_zh: 叙拉古“狄奥尼修斯之耳”
object: The “Ear of Dionysius”, an artificial cave cut into the wall of the Latomia del Paradiso, Neapolis archaeological park, Syracuse, Sicily. Photographed 2025.
author: Julian Lupyan
attribution_text: Photo: Julian Lupyan / CC0, via Wikimedia Commons

title_zh: 从普尼克斯讲坛望卫城
title_en: The Acropolis from the speakers' platform on the Pnyx
object: View from the orator's bema on the Pnyx, meeting place of the Athenian assembly, toward the Acropolis and Mount Lycabettus, Athens. Photographed 23 September 2018.
author: George E. Koronaios
attribution_text: Photo: George E. Koronaios / CC0, via Wikimedia Commons

title_zh: 雅典长墙遗迹（莫斯哈托）
title_en: Remains of the Long Walls at Moschato
object: Remains of the Long Walls between Athens and Piraeus, preserved in a park in Moschato, Attica. Photographed 25 February 2019.
author: George E. Koronaios
attribution_text: Photo: George E. Koronaios / CC0, via Wikimedia Commons

title_zh: 比雷埃夫斯泽亚港古代遗迹
title_en: Ancient remains at Zea harbour, Piraeus
object: Ancient remains (possibly fortifications) at the harbour of Zea, Piraeus, the main naval base of classical Athens. Photographed 24 February 2019.
author: George E. Koronaios
attribution_text: Photo: George E. Koronaios / CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

title_zh: 赫尔墨斯方柱像（“门前的赫尔墨斯”）
object: Marble herm inscribed as a copy of the Hermes Propylaios by Alkamenes (original 5th c. BC, at the entrance to the Athenian Acropolis); Roman copy of the 2nd c. AD, probably from Pergamon. The head may not belong to the inscribed shaft. Istanbul Archaeology Museums, Inv. 1433.
author: Marie-Lan Nguyen
attribution_text: Photo: © Marie-Lan Nguyen / Wikimedia Commons / CC BY 4.0

title_zh: 赫尔墨斯方柱像头部（雅典古市集博物馆）
title_en: Herm head of Hermes (Ancient Agora Museum)
object: Marble head from a herm of Hermes, ca. 425 BC. Museum of the Ancient Agora, Athens.
author: Zde
attribution_text: Photo: Zde / CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

title_zh: 派罗斯之战缴获的斯巴达青铜盾
title_en: Spartan bronze shield captured at Pylos
object: Bronze facing of a Spartan shield taken as booty by the Athenians at Pylos/Sphacteria in 425 BC, with a punched dedicatory inscription (“The Athenians from the Lacedaemonians from Pylos”). Museum of the Ancient Agora, Athens.
author: Dorieo (Jerónimo Roure Pérez)
attribution_text: Photo: Dorieo, Wikimedia Commons / CC BY-SA 4.0
